numeral.purpose: The figure that leads a block: step numbers, 45 minutes, Free, 40%.

price.purpose: A price on its pattern piece, sized so the narrowest piece fits $129.

body.purpose: Running text, capped at the 38rem measure.

motion.name: ease-draw
motion.purpose: Default timing for every transition (colour swaps).

motion.name: default-transition-duration
motion.purpose: Flat colour swaps on links and notched buttons.

motion.name: seam-draw
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0); linear; animation-timeline: view(block 0 25%); range entry-crossing 0% to 100%
motion.purpose: The home page's long chalk seam drawing on scroll. Only with prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and animation-timeline support; otherwise drawn whole and static.

patternMarks.seam: SVG stroke in chalk, width 2.25, dasharray 8 6, non-scaling.
patternMarks.notch: Small triangle cut into an edge, filled with the colour behind; 14px, or 10 by 16 on the step list. Buttons: 0.75rem wide, 0.5rem deep, 1.5rem from the right edge.
patternMarks.grainline: Vertical double arrow in chalk, stroke 2.25, rounded caps.
patternMarks.punchedHole: 22px chalk ring, stroke 2.25; filled navy on /pricing pieces, hanging from a chalk cord.
patternMarks.todo: 1.5px dashed currentColor outline, 0.3em inline padding, box-decoration-break clone.
patternMarks.ruled: Hard-edged 2px lines on a 2.25rem pitch, background-attachment local, colour via --rule-color.

narrative.overview:
The site is a tailor's working pattern, marked by a hand you're about to meet. Every marketing page is mostly one flat ochre card laid on a navy cutting table. Sections are pieces cut from that card: their top edges carry real garment geometry (a neck curve, a shoulder slope, an armhole), drawn as inline SVG and rising over the piece before them. On the card, chalk draws the working marks: a dashed seam allowance inside each cut edge, triangular notches, a grainline double arrow, a punched hole. Timber is the Saigon ground, and the only sections set on it are the ones about Saigon.

The world is flat, square and specific. There are no shadows, no radii, no soft gradients and no decorative motion; depth comes from one piece of card sitting on another, and a piece only sits on one that comes earlier in the process. Numbers carry the persuasion: $890, 40%, 45 minutes and Free are set in Besley numerals as the largest thing in their block. Unfilled facts stay visible as dashed `[TODO]` outlines, like a fitter's open question, rather than being hidden or invented.

It refuses the luxury tailor (dark photography, hushed serif, gold) and the previous site (cream ground, high-contrast serif, red accent, hairlines). It is warm, plain and working, and it should never read as "too luxury".
keyCharacteristics: One committed colour: flat ochre card over navy table, with timber for Saigon and chalk for lines and form surfaces.
Section edges are cut pattern geometry, never rectangles with a divider.
Chalk marks are drawn lines: dashed seams, notches, grainline, punched hole. A few per section, not many.
Lantern red appears only where someone books.
Two faces: Besley for headings and numerals, Be Vietnam Pro for everything else.
Square corners, no shadows; hover is a flat colour swap.
One gesture moves: the home page's long chalk seam draws itself on scroll.

rules.name: The Lantern Is For Booking Rule
rules.body: Lantern red is for booking actions and nothing else: never a line, stripe, border or decoration on the card. The one sanctioned exception is form validation on `/contact` (owner decision), where errors also carry words and a notch mark so colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Chalk Is a Line Rule
rules.body: Chalk on ochre is about 2:1, so chalk on the card is for drawn lines only, never text. Text on ochre is always navy (about 7:1); on ochre-deep it is navy (about 6:1).

rules.name: The Surface Declares Rule
rules.body: Every section declares exactly one surface: card, chalk, table or timber. The surface sets its text colour, focus-ring colour, selection colour and link-swap pair together; never set those piecemeal. Card and chalk swap to navy with chalk text; table and timber swap to ochre with navy text.

rules.name: The Flag Guard Rule
rules.body: Ochre with red sits close to two Vietnamese flags: never a star on red, and never three parallel stripes of any colour on ochre.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Besley and Be Vietnam Pro, nothing else. No third face and no fake handwriting: chalk marks are drawn lines, and words stay in these two faces.

rules.name: The Numbers Lead Rule
rules.body: A block's figure is set in Besley numerals and is the biggest thing in that block, with a visible label beside it. Only one figure leads per block; supporting figures step down to heading size. On home, `$890` alone leads the first screen.

rules.name: The Lighter Zero Rule
rules.body: Never use `tabular-nums` on Besley; its tabular zero is visibly lighter. Where figures must align, put each digit in a fixed-width cell (0.62em) and give screen readers the whole string.

rules.name: The No Label Caps Rule
rules.body: No tracked uppercase labels and no eyebrows above headings. Weight and size carry hierarchy.

rules.name: The Overlap Means Order Rule
rules.body: One piece overlaps another only when it comes later in the process. Nothing overlaps for decoration.

rules.name: The Always Located Rule
rules.body: A section names its city wherever the content says so, and Saigon content sits on timber.

rules.name: The Flat Card Rule
rules.body: No box shadows, drop shadows, glows, blur or glass, ever. If something needs to read as on top, cut its edge over what it covers.

rules.name: The One Gesture Rule
rules.body: The chalk seam is the only thing that moves on scroll, anywhere on the site. Everything else is still apart from 120ms colour swaps, and `prefers-reduced-motion` reduces all animation and transition to near zero and turns off smooth scrolling.

rules.name: The Open Question Rule
rules.body: A missing fact is shown as a dashed `[TODO]`, never hidden, softened or invented.

dos: **Do** declare one surface per section (card, chalk, table or timber) and let it set text, focus, selection and link swap.
**Do** cut section edges from the pattern vocabulary (shoulder, collar, armhole, neck, hem) with a chalk seam inside, rising `hem` over the piece before.
**Do** keep text on ochre navy; chalk on the card is for lines only.
**Do** reserve lantern for booking actions (and `/contact` field errors, with words and a notch mark).
**Do** set leading figures in Besley numerals as the biggest thing in their block, with a visible label.
**Do** make every hover a flat colour swap and every corner square.
**Do** show unfilled facts with the dashed `[TODO]` outline, and empty photos as a labelled deep-ochre slot with a chalk-dashed outline.
**Do** design at 390 by 844 first; the photo slot gives way before the tagline, offer and price.
**Do** put Saigon on timber, and name a section's city wherever the content does.
donts: **Don't** use shadows, radii, pills, glass, glows, or colour gradients. The ruled message field's hard-edged lines are drawn lines, not a gradient fill.
**Don't** use tracked uppercase labels or eyebrows above headings.
**Don't** add a third typeface, handwriting fonts, icon-library icons or emoji; all marks are drawn in this repo as inline SVG.
**Don't** use lantern red as a line, stripe or decoration, put a star on red, or lay three parallel stripes on ochre.
**Don't** overlap pieces for decoration; a piece only sits on one that comes later in the process.
**Don't** add scroll or entrance animation beyond the chalk seam.
**Don't** lay out a row of identical cards; price pieces differ in shape and size.
**Don't** drift toward luxury (dark photo grounds, gold, hushed serif) or back to the old site (cream ground, red accent, hairlines). Chalk stays cool (#f0f3f4), never cream.
**Don't** draw people or figures on the pattern pieces, or imply in visuals or copy that the workshop uses paper patterns unless the owner confirms it.
